html: Cells remove reactive oxygen species in two steps. Superoxide, made by NADPH oxidases and mitochondria, is dismutated to hydrogen peroxide by the superoxide dismutases, SOD1 in the cytosol (loaded with copper by its chaperone CCS), SOD2 in mitochondria and SOD3 outside the cell. Hydrogen peroxide is then reduced to water by catalase, by the glutathione peroxidases, which use glutathione regenerated by glutathione reductase and NADPH, and by the peroxiredoxins, which are reduced again by thioredoxin and thioredoxin reductase. Superoxide that meets nitric oxide first forms peroxynitrite, a strong oxidant.
